_comment: PROTOTYPE SEED — a simulated distributor, not a set of UI test cases. A product master, a 12-customer book, 90 days of trading, a replenishment policy and a purchase pipeline were simulated; stock, batch expiry, demand, velocity and every classification fall out of that. No SKU was authored to be short, overstocked or declining — those are consequences of its trend, its buyer's ordering and its shelf life. ALL OF IT IS ILLUSTRATIVE: there is no sales history and no promised delivery date in the real source systems (model addendum-003 §9), which is exactly what this stands in for. Sales history is generated from a base rate, an annualised trend, a weekday shape and noise; run rates are measured from it rather than assigned. Demand is the sum of open order lines by promised delivery date. Batches are receipts consumed oldest-first by the sales that actually happened, so expiry spread, mixed-batch SKUs and expired stock all emerge. Untraced stock represents legacy transfers and manual counts that arrived without a batch. Cost is landed purchase cost; a SKU with no batch has no cost basis and is excluded from every rupee figure. See addendum-006.

policy._note: PROTOTYPE BUSINESS POLICY, not a rule discovered in the data. Target stock = replenishment-period demand + safety stock, both from the SKU's own 30-day run rate. Sellable/target above 1.25 reads Overstock, below 0.75 Understocked.
